TWO SPHERICAL CONDUCTORS.
225
Let $a$ and $b$ be the radii of the spheres, and $c$ the distance
between their centres. We shall also, for the sake of brevity,
write $a=c x$, and $b=c y$, so that $x$ and $y$ are numerical quantities
less than unity.
Let the line joining the centres of the spheres be taken as
the axis of the zonal harmonics, and let the pole of the zonal
harmonics belonging to either sphere be the point of that sphere
nearest to the other.
Let $r$ be the distance of any point from the centre of the first
sphere, and $s$ the distance of the same point from that of the
second sphere.
Let the surface density, $\sigma_{1}$, of the first sphere be given by the
equation
$$4 \pi \sigma_{1} a^{2}=A+A_{1} P_{1}+3 A_{2} P_{2}+\text { \&c. }+(2 m+1) A_{m} P_{m}$$
(1)
so that $A$ is the total charge of the sphere, and $A_{1}$, \&c. are the
coefficients of the zonal harmonics $P_{1}$, \&c.
The potential due to this distribution of charge may be repre-
sented by
$$U^{\prime}=\frac{1}{a}\left[A+A_{1} I_{1}^{\prime} \frac{r}{a}+A_{2} P_{2} \frac{r^{2}}{a^{2}}+\text { \&c. }+A_{m} P_{m}^{r^{m}}\right]$$
(2)
for points inside the sphere, and by
$$U=\frac{1}{r}\left[A+A_{1} P_{1} \frac{a}{r}+A_{2} I_{2} \frac{a^{2}}{r^{2}}+\text { \&c. }+A_{m} P_{m} \frac{a^{m}}{r^{m}}\right]$$
(3)
for points outside.
Similarly, if the surface density on the second sphere is given
by the equation
$$4 \pi \sigma_{2} b^{2}=B+B_{1} P_{1}+\text { \&c. }+(2 n+1) B_{n} P_{n}$$
(4)
the potential inside and outside this sphere due to this charge
may be represented by equations of the form
$$\begin{aligned}
V^{\prime} & =\frac{1}{b}\left[B+B_{1} 1_{1} \frac{s}{b}+\text { \&c. }+B_{n} P_{n} \frac{s^{n}}{b^{n}}\right] \\
V & =\frac{1}{s}\left[B+B_{1} P_{1} \frac{b}{s}+\text { \&c. }+B_{n} P_{n} \frac{b^{n}}{s^{n}}\right]
\end{aligned}$$
(5)
(6)
where the several harmonics are related to the second sphere.
The charges of the spheres are $A$ and $B$ respectively.
The potential at every point within the first sphere is constant
and equal to $a$, the potential of that sphere, so that within the
first sphere
$$U^{\prime}+V=a .$$
(7)
vol. i.

 less than unity.


Let the line joining the centres of the spheres be taken as
 the axis of the zonal harmonics, and let the pole of the zonal
 harmonics belonging to either sphere be the point of that sphere
 nearest to the other.


Let $r$ be the distance of any point from the centre of the first
 sphere, and $s$ the distance of the same point from that of the
 second sphere.


Let the surface density, $\sigma_{1}$, of the first sphere be given by the
 equation

$$\begin{equation*}
4 \pi \sigma_{1} a^{2}=A+A_{1} P_{1}+3 A_{2} P_{2}+\text { \&c. }+(2 m+1) A_{m} P_{m} \tag{1}
\end{equation*}$$

so that $A$ is the total charge of the sphere, and $A_{1}$, \&c. are the
 coefficients of the zonal harmonics $P_{1}$, \&c.


The potential due to this distribution of charge may be repre
sented by

$$\begin{equation*}
U^{\prime}=\frac{1}{a}\left[A+A_{1} I_{1}^{\prime} \frac{r}{a}+A_{2} P_{2} \frac{r^{2}}{a^{2}}+\text { \&c. }+A_{m} P_{m}^{r^{m}}\right] \tag{2}
\end{equation*}$$

for points inside the sphere, and by

$$\begin{equation*}
U=\frac{1}{r}\left[A+A_{1} P_{1} \frac{a}{r}+A_{2} I_{2} \frac{a^{2}}{r^{2}}+\text { \&c. }+A_{m} P_{m} \frac{a^{m}}{r^{m}}\right] \tag{3}
\end{equation*}$$

for points outside.

Similarly, if the surface density on the second sphere is given
 by the equation

$$\begin{equation*}
4 \pi \sigma_{2} b^{2}=B+B_{1} P_{1}+\text { \&c. }+(2 n+1) B_{n} P_{n} \tag{4}
\end{equation*}$$

the potential inside and outside this sphere due to this charge
 may be represented by equations of the form

$$\begin{align*}
V^{\prime} & =\frac{1}{b}\left[B+B_{1} 1_{1} \frac{s}{b}+\text { \&c. }+B_{n} P_{n} \frac{s^{n}}{b^{n}}\right]  \tag{5}\\
V & =\frac{1}{s}\left[B+B_{1} P_{1} \frac{b}{s}+\text { \&c. }+B_{n} P_{n} \frac{b^{n}}{s^{n}}\right] \tag{6}
\end{align*}$$

where the several harmonics are related to the second sphere.

The charges of the spheres are $A$ and $B$ respectively.

The potential at every point within the first sphere is constant
 and equal to $a$, the potential of that sphere, so that within the
 first sphere

$$\begin{equation*}
U^{\prime}+V=a . \tag{7}
\end{equation*}$$
